title: Replace raw e.toString() exception text in settings error messages with the project's own ST-4 friendly-error pattern
rule: EH-5 / custom_lint no_e_to_string_in_ui (currently non-enforcing per tooling gap)
why: curriculum_settings_screen.dart:79, lifetime_marking_screen.dart:606, account_actions.dart:401(state)/468(render), account_actions.dart:579, and send_logs_service.dart:104 all interpolate the raw Dart exception's toString() into a message shown to the user -- account_actions.dart:468 has no l10n wrapper at all. A Hebrew-speaking parent or child sees a half-English, technical string (exception class names, network error codes) instead of a real message. This is inconsistent with the SAME batch's own upgrade_to_cloud_screen.dart, which explicitly names and implements the pattern to avoid this ('Never surface the raw exception... mirrors the ST-4 friendly-error pattern', upgrade_to_cloud_screen.dart:198-200) -- proving the project already knows how to do this correctly elsewhere.
recommendation: Replace each e.toString() interpolation with a fixed, already-localized fallback string per the ST-4 pattern used in upgrade_to_cloud_screen.dart/backup_sync_section.dart; log the real exception via AppLogger for diagnostics instead of showing it.
acceptance_criteria: None of the 5 sites pass exception content into Text(...)/ARB placeholders; a grep-based check for `.toString())` inside `l10n.`/`Text(` call sites in lib/features/settings can gate regressions once custom_lint's no_e_to_string_in_ui rule is repaired.
Widget test with Locale('he') asserts each error surface renders only ARB-sourced Hebrew text, never a mocked exception's message.
